# Check of the Actium animation against the stored passages

**Checked:** 2026-11-24, by Claude Code, for the curator.
**What was checked:** `Actium Campaign and Battle, 31 BC (Animated Terrain Map).html` in this folder: 13 steps, each with an account and an "ancient source" locator.
**Its origin** (curator, 2026-11-24): generated by Claude in a chat, from the Wikipedia article "Battle of Actium".
**Checked against:** the passages stored in the graph:
- Plutarch, *Life of Antony*, tr. Perrin: 56 passages;
- Cassius Dio, *Roman History*, tr. Cary: 116 passages;
- Velleius Paterculus: 15 passages.

**Result:** the scene draft [`scenes/actium-campaign-31bc.proposed.json`](../../scenes/actium-campaign-31bc.proposed.json). Every statement in it carries its basis, and every quotation was checked verbatim against the stored passage.

## Where its detail comes from

Most of the animation's detail is **not** in the Wikipedia revision we hold (1378178531). That revision cites Dio only five times (50.13, 50.23.1, 50.31, 50.32, 51.1). It has none of Bogud, Nasidius, Toryne, Leucas, Taenarum, Coelius, Cleopatra's sixty ships, the right wing backing water, the eight furlongs, or the seven days. The detail and the precise locators came from the generating model's own knowledge, or from a later revision. They were claimed, not read, so each one was checked here.

## Step by step

| # | Step (animation's locator) | Verdict | What our passages say |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Antony holds western Greece (Dio 50.9.3) | **Partly; locator not held** | 50.9.3 is not held, so the winter at Patrae is unchecked. Garrisons at Corcyra (Dio 50.12.2) and Methone (50.11.3) are confirmed. "Guarding the route from Egypt" is the generator's inference. |
| 2 | Agrippa storms Methone (Dio 50.11.3) | **Confirmed**, one addition | Methone stormed, Bogud killed, merchant ships watched, raids on Greece. "Grain ships from Egypt" is not in the passage; Dio says "merchant vessels". |
| 3 | Octavian crosses (Dio 50.11.5–12.3; Plut. 62.3) | **Confirmed**, order simplified | The crossing (50.11.6), the cavalry at the Ceraunian mountains (50.12.1), Corcyra (50.12.2), Toryne (Plut. 62.3), and the high ground where Nicopolis stood (50.12.3–4). "Marches south" is inferred. |
| 4 | Agrippa closes the ring (Dio 50.13.5; Vell. 2.84.2) | **Confirmed** | Leucas, Patrae (Nasidius beaten at sea) and Corinth, in both sources. Disease and desertion: Dio 50.11.2, Vell. 2.84.1. "Short of food" is not in a passage read here. |
| 5 | The fleets form up (Plut. 65; Dio 50.31) | **Confirmed; caption corrected** | Line "a little outside the strait" (Dio 50.31.4). "About eight furlongs" (Plut. 65.4), so 1.5 km is right. A long wait (65.4; Dio 50.31.5). Cleopatra **in the rear** (Plut. 66.3; Dio 50.33.1); "behind the centre" is the generator's. |
| 6 | Antony's left moves first (Plut. 65.4–5) | **Confirmed** | The sixth hour, a sea wind, Antony's left in motion, Octavian's right rowing backwards. |
| 7 | Agrippa stretches the wing (Plut. 66.3) | **Confirmed** | Exact. "Northern" is the map's compass point. |
| 8 | Cleopatra breaks out (Plut. 66.5; Dio 50.33.1–3) | **Confirmed; locator mapped** | Our 66.3–4. Dio 50.33.2 reads it as panic; the graph's Questions hold the debate. |
| 9 | Antony follows (Plut. 66.7; Dio 50.33.3) | **Confirmed; one line corrected** | Our 66.5: a five-oared galley, with Alexas and Scellius. **"The fleet loses its treasury" is contradicted:** Dio 50.34.1 and 50.35.5 have the money still aboard the ships left fighting. |
| 10 | The fleet left behind is destroyed (Dio 50.34–35; Plut. 68.1) | **Confirmed** | Fire from the camp (Dio). The tenth hour, a high sea, 300 ships captured (Plut.). The two sources differ on what ended it; both are kept. |
| 11 | The army goes over (Plut. 68.3) | **Confirmed; order corrected** | Seven days first, **then** Canidius flees by night, then the army goes over. |
| 12 | Flight to Taenarum, then Egypt (Plut. 67; 69.1) | **Partly; 69.1 not held** | Taken aboard (67.1); from Taenarum to Libya (67.6); the Peloponnese, then Egypt (Dio 51.5.3). Paraetonium is unchecked. |
| 13 | Alexandria falls, 1 Aug 30 BC (Plut. 76–86; Dio 51.10–15) | **Mostly not held** | Cleopatra's burial (Plut. 86.4) is held. Antony's death, the capture of the city and the date are not. |

## Disagreements the animation flattened

- **Antony's left wing:** Plutarch has Coelius (65.1). Velleius only says the fleet was entrusted to Publicola and Sosius (2.85.2) and gives Sosius no wing. "Coelius south (Velleius: Sosius)" was the generator's reading.
- **Octavian's order of battle:** Plutarch has Agrippa on the left, Octavian on the right and Arruntius in the centre (65.2, 66.3). Velleius has Lurius on the right and Arruntius on the left, with Agrippa over the whole (2.85.2). The scene keeps both orders as alternatives.

## Locators

The animation numbers Plutarch's chapter 66 differently from our Perrin text: its 66.5 and 66.7 are our 66.3 and 66.5. The scene cites our numbering and notes the mapping.

## Not held: to read

Dio 50.9.3 and 51.10–13; Plutarch 69.1 and 76–85. Harvesting these is extraction and needs no review. It would settle steps 1, 12 and 13.

## Places named but not in the graph

Brundisium, Corcyra, Toryne, Leucas, Methone, Taenarum and Paraetonium. The scene carries the animation's points for them, marked unverified, until the gazetteer adds them from Pleiades. Patrae is held under its modern name, Patras, so the scene shows the ancient name. Octavian's camp has no coordinates on its card.

## Resolved the same day

- **Passages read** (migration 034, extraction only):
  - Dio 50.9.3, 50.14.4, 51.10.1, 51.10.4, 51.10.7, 51.10.9 and 51.19.6;
  - Plutarch 69.1, 76.1, 76.2, 76.3, 77.1 and 80.1.
  - What they settle:
    - Step 1: the winter at Patrae, and the soldiers spread to guard the strategic points (Dio 50.9.3).
    - Step 4: "short of food" (Dio 50.14.4).
    - Step 12: Paraetonium (Plutarch 69.1; Dio 51.10.1).
    - Step 13: the fleet's desertion, Antony's death, and Octavian entering the city.
- **A new disagreement:** Plutarch 69.1 has Cleopatra go on to Egypt **from Paraetonium**, with Antony, while Dio 51.5.3 has her hasten to Egypt from the Peloponnese. The scene keeps both routes.
- **Still unsourced:** the date, 1 August 30 BC. Dio 51.19.6 says only that the day of the capture was declared a lucky day.
- **Places added** (migration 035, proposed):
  - Brundisium, Toryne, Leucas, Methone, Taenarum and Paraetonium, each from the passage that names it, with its Pleiades record and Location.
  - Corcyra is the graph's existing Corfu, the island.
  - Which Pleiades record answers to the passage's place is a reading, and stays for the curator.
- **The scene** now has 44 sourced statements, 5 inferred and 1 not checked.
